scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: The makers-fair guide has an early draft and a teacher-approved revision. After a pretend device failure, Neel finds a file with the right name but the old contents. Tara asks both where the copy survived and which version the team actually needs.
scenes.speech: The makers-fair guide has an early draft and a teacher-approved revision. After a pretend device failure, Neel finds a file with the right name but the old contents. Tara asks both where the copy survived and which version the team actually needs.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: Version describes the contents at a particular stage; location describes where a copy is kept. Two versions on the same lost laptop may both become unavailable. A separate approved backup can survive that loss, but it still needs a check for completeness and the correct revision.
scenes.speech: Version describes the contents at a particular stage; location describes where a copy is kept. Two versions on the same lost laptop may both become unavailable. A separate approved backup can survive that loss, but it still needs a check for completeness and the correct revision.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: The teacher restores a copy into a test location without overwriting the only original. The class opens it and compares the approved diagram and pages. A successful filename or progress bar is not enough: the recovered work must be usable and meet the stated requirement.
scenes.speech: The teacher restores a copy into a test location without overwriting the only original. The class opens it and compares the approved diagram and pages. A successful filename or progress bar is not enough: the recovered work must be usable and meet the stated requirement.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: The team needs the approved revision. One recovered copy opens but contains the old draft; another matches the teacher’s approved pages. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.speech: The team needs the approved revision. One recovered copy opens but contains the old draft; another matches the teacher’s approved pages. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.dialogue: Which recovered file meets the stated need?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: Use the tested copy matching the approved revision and retain the recovery record. Being able to open an old draft does not mean the current work has been restored.
scenes.speech: Use the tested copy matching the approved revision and retain the recovery record. Being able to open an old draft does not mean the current work has been restored.
scenes.dialogue: Choose a backup surviving the stated loss.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate version and location, then a separate backup, then a tested restoration. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.speech: Investigate version and location, then a separate backup, then a tested restoration. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.dialogue: How can a backup survive a lost device but still fail the recovery goal?
